The quote states the GENERAL FDA-approved adult dose of moxifloxacin (400 mg q24h, oral or IV), applicable to its labeled indications (CAP, sinusitis, skin/skin-structure, intra-abdominal infection). verify.refute_attempt: REFUTATION: The byte_quote appears verbatim on the page, and the re-extracted dose (400 mg IV q24h) is byte-accurate. HOWEVER, the dose is NOT grounded to bacterial meningitis. The label is the FDA prescribing information for AVELOX (moxifloxacin), and the quoted sentence is the GENERAL dosing statement that applies uniformly to ALL six approved indications. Confirmed: the word "meningitis" does NOT appear anywhere on the page (checked twice); neither do "CNS infection," "plague," or "anthrax." The complete INDICATIONS AND USAGE list is: acute bacterial sinusitis, acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis, community-acquired pneumonia, uncomplicated skin/skin-structure infections, complicated intra-abdominal infections, and complicated skin/skin-structure infections. None is meningitis or any CNS/intrathecal indication. The label even flags CNS issues only as ADVERSE reactions (seizures, hallucinations), not as a treatable indication. The single "400 mg once every 24 hours" dose is therefore the dose for these labeled (mostly respiratory/skin/abdominal) indications — it is the standard systemic dose, not a meningitis-specific or CNS-penetration-validated dose. The CLAIM that this is the "dose for adult bacterial meningitis" / "beta-lactam-sparing agent" for meningitis is an EXTRAPOLATION/off-label inference that this FDA source does NOT state. The byte_quote is real; the meningitis-specific clinical attribution is unsupported by the cited page.
